newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt, futures firm ahead of April jobs data.
newsitem.headline: German debt, futures firm ahead of April jobs data.

text.p: German Bunds and futures were modestly firmer in late dealings on Monday that were marked by thin volumes due to a British banking holiday, traders said.
At 1430 GMT, DTB June Bund futures were up 18 basis points at 101.78 points and had traded less than 30,000 contracts while being confined to a range from 101.69 to 101.88 points.
The benchmark 10-year cash Bund due July 2007 was at 101.73 points with a yield of 5.76 percent, up from 100.48 on Friday.
The market was range-bound as London markets were closed and ahead of Tuesday's German April jobless report, which sources said will show a drop in unadjusted terms.

German unemployment in April fell in unadjusted terms to 4.347 million, or 11.3 percent of the workforce, from 4.477 in March, or 11.7 percent, according to sources who have access to official data to be released on Tuesday.
Sources told Reuters the number of people out of work in west Germany slipped to 3.031 million, or 9.8 percent, and east German jobless totals fell to 1.315 million, or 17.5 percent.
In March, west German jobless totals were 3.127 million, an unemployment rate of 9.8 percent, and in east Germany 1.350 million people were out of work, a rate of 18.1 percent.
The figures are not adjusted for seasonal influences.
The Federal Labour Office is scheduled to release the official data at a news conference in Nuremberg on Tuesday.
Market analysts said the data would likely be above market expectations based on the leaked data.

"First leaks from tomorrow's April unemployment report suggests the data will be less good news for the economy as is currently anticipated by the market," market analyst group MMS International said in a commentary.
On a technical basis, traders said June futures support is at 101.61, with a break of that level offering support at 101.43. Resistance is seen at 101.88, the day's session high.
